title: Traffic orchestration: region-priority fallback with geo-pin and capacity-aware shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a production-safe traffic orchestration policy that combines latency-based routing, configurable geo-pinning, and capacity-aware failover with integrated circuit-breaking and load-shedding hooks.
Goal: keep latency SLOs for tiered customers while preventing regional overload and ensuring graceful degradation (model-size fallbacks and retry hedging) during capacity pressure or region outages.
This ticket designs the policy, implements the runtime decision path, and adds monitoring/alerting and rollout controls in Console for per-customer overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Policy implemented in router with unit + integration tests: deterministic outcomes for deterministic inputs and probabilistic outcomes within configured error bounds for weighted fallbacks
E2E test demonstrating failover from primary region -> secondary region under simulated capacity pressure with <2x latency increase for P0 customers and <3x for P1 customers
Circuit breaker metrics emitted (tripped_count, open_duration, trips_per_minute) and dashboard with SLO burn rate per region
Load-shedding action executes defined plan: step 1 reduce batching/decrease tokens, step 2 route to smaller model variant, step 3 reject with graceful response code and telemetry
Console controls for geo-pin lists and capacity thresholds exposed and documented
Rollout plan validated via canary (5% traffic) with automatic rollback on error budget increase
design_decisions: Latency base: use 95th percentile observed p95 over rolling 5m as routing signal (not instantaneous p50) to avoid oscillation
Capacity hint: each region provides continuous 'available_units' metric (GPU capacity equivalents). Router gears to remaining capacity fraction, not just queue length
Geo-pin: default behavior is soft-pin (weight boost) rather than hard-pin; eligible requests can opt-out via header for special-cases
Fallback ordering: prefer same-region smaller model variant -> nearby region with capacity -> global pool, with probabilistic weighted routing to avoid synchronized bursts
Circuit-breaker granularity: per-region-per-customer-per-model-family to avoid noisy neighbors; thresholds computed from historical normal traffic and scaled by customer tier
Load-shedding policy: deterministic ranked actions (reduce batch, reduce max_tokens, switch quantized variant, reject with 429+structured payload) executed with minimum disruption
Backoff/hedge: on transient routing failures issue hedged request to the second-choice target after configurable jittered delay
implementation_notes: Router changes: add policy engine module 'orchestrator' with inputs: p95_latency[region], available_units[region], geo_distance_score, customer_tier, model_family
Wire 'capacity-hint' into service discovery layer from dedicated capacity exporter (ENG-39721 will add the exporter). Temporary mock available_units used for local testing
New config schema: region_priority_rules (list), pin_mode (hard|soft), fallback_sequence (list), breaker_thresholds (percentages and absolute minima), shedding_actions (ordered list)
Add unit tests for decision matrix and property-based tests for stochastic weighted fallback to validate distribution over 10k simulated requests
Add integration harness that replays production traces with synthetic region outages to validate policy behavior
Add migration that defaults existing customers to previous behavior (latency-first without capacity hints) and enables new policy per-customer via Console toggle
testing_plan: Local: run router unit tests and property tests; use synthetic available_units variations to exercise shedding pathways
Staging: replay 48h of production traffic evenly split across regions; inject capacity drain events and assert canary SLOs
Chaos: schedule controlled region failover during staging with circuit-breaker trip simulation and verify hedging or fallback triggers
Load test: ramp to 200% of baseline regional peak and verify that shedding actions reduce QPS and maintain p95 SLO for P0 customers within configured budget
Post-deploy smoke checks: verify metrics emission and that Console toggles work end-to-end
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics to emit: routing_decision{source_region,target_region,model_family}, p95_routing_latency, available_units_fraction, breaker_state{region,customer,model_family}, shedding_action_executed
Dashboards: per-region SLO burn rate, per-customer error budget, histogram of fallback hop counts, time-series of shedding actions
Alerts: fire at 10% SLO burn rate sustained 5m (warn) and 50% sustained 1m (critical), and when a breaker trips >10 times/min for a region
Runbook: documented steps to diagnose expected cause (network vs capacity vs model overload) and safe mitigations (scale up Dedicated, reduce batching globally, whitelist customer pin)
Log context: include decision rationale in traces (selected_reason, candidate_scores, available_units_snapshot) for offline postmortems
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable 5% traffic for internal customers in us-west-2 for 48h, auto-rollback if SLO burn increases beyond threshold
Phase 2 (gradual): 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 1 week with metrics gate checks at each step
Phase 3 (per-customer opt-in): enable Console toggle for safety-critical customers to preview soft-pin behavior
Phase 4 (global): flip default for new customers and monitor for 2 weeks before migrating existing customers
Fallback plan: immediate global rollback path documented with config flag and kill-switch in Console
